spot.html_text: It is evident that the law of karma is taken as an extension of the law of causation that governs the physical world to the sphere of human conduct. This view is compatible with a version of self-determinism. We have seen that to explain the phenomenon of remote causation, Indian philosophers have posited adṛṣṭa—the potency produced as a consequence of one’s action(s) and which is non-eternal like any produced object. spot.html_text: The imperceptible part of the smallest visible thing must possess parts, if it is a composite thing. However, this division of composite things into its parts must come to an end; otherwise there will be a vicious infinite regress (anavasthā). So, there must be partless, indivisible, imperceptible things, things which are defined as atoms.
